we show that there exists a putatively error signal reflected in the intracortically recorded neural activity of the human hand region of motor cortex, that can be utilized to develop an automatic error detect-and-und system for intracortically controlled brain-computer interfaces.

there exists a putatitive error signal reflected in the neural activity of the human hand motor cortex and that this error signal can be decoded with very high accuracy, which suggests that it will be feasible to implement a real-time error detection and correction system in human clinical intracortial BCIs.

developing the next generation of BCI systems that can automatically detect errors in real-time, and correct them without user intervention.
improving the performance of intracortical brain–computer interfaces (iBCIs) by developing an automatic error detect-and- undo system.
improving the performance of human intracortical brain–computer interfaces (hBCIs) by detecting and correcting movement errors.
